decisions.reason: The charting bundle was publicly launched and actively released as part of the map.apps platform, so management will keep it as a committed component despite no visibility since 2019.
The hierarchical search bundle carries little visible commitment and has not been observed since 2018, but as a cheap plugin on the core platform it can still be justified as temporarily low-profile.
VueTOC was announced on the home page, which leaves a public commitment to justify, though as an experimental mobile component it is the most likely to be absorbed into other offerings.
The GIS platform is the flagship product line and central to the announced strategy, so heavy investment and public commitment make persistence near certain.
The field data capture software has a dedicated page and fits the core offer, so weak visibility can be attributed to temporary adoption delays.
The search extension has its own page and belongs to the committed web map ecosystem, so management will keep it even though it has not been seen recently.
